frontmatter.description: Authenticate the Lakekeeper Python and Java clients with OAuth2 bearer tokens, and choose the right strategy for scripts, services and notebooks.
Catalog non-Iceberg data — Lance, Parquet, CSV and any other format — alongside Iceberg tables with Lakekeeper's format-agnostic Generic Table API.

Configure Lakekeeper Warehouses on AWS S3 and S3-compatible storage such as MinIO, SeaweedFS, Cloudflare R2 and Alibaba Cloud OSS: parameters, credentials, STS vended credentials, remote signing and CORS.
Configure Lakekeeper Warehouses on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2: parameters, App Registration and storage account setup, SAS vended credentials and Azure system identities.
Configure Lakekeeper Warehouses on Google Cloud Storage: parameters, service account keys, GCP system identities, downscoped vended credentials and CORS.

Configure Lakekeeper Warehouses on OneLake (Microsoft Fabric) lakehouses: parameters, endpoint modes and private links, Entra credentials, the Fabric settings for user-delegated SAS tokens, path restrictions and client versions.

Configure Lakekeeper Warehouses on STACKIT Object Storage: storage services, credentials groups and trust policies for STS, bucket policies that keep other credentials groups out, CORS and troubleshooting.
Connect Spark, Trino, StarRocks, DuckDB, Athena, Flink, PyIceberg and other query engines, and ingestion tools such as OLake Go, to Lakekeeper's Iceberg REST Catalog with per-user permissions.
Control how Lakekeeper lays out namespace and table directories under a Warehouse location: the default, full-hierarchy and tabular-only layouts, name and UUID templates, and namespace moves.
How Lakekeeper Warehouses store data: storage profiles and credentials, the supported object stores (S3, STACKIT, ADLS, OneLake, GCS), table locations, credential vending, remote signing and CORS.
Interactive OpenAPI reference for Lakekeeper's Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API.
Interactive OpenAPI reference for Lakekeeper's Generic Table API for non-Iceberg table formats.
Overview of Lakekeeper's three HTTP APIs: the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API, the Generic Table API and the Management API, plus the built-in Swagger UI.
Read and write Lance generic tables from PySpark using the Lakekeeper client and short-lived, prefix-scoped vended storage credentials.
Stream data from Apache Flink into Lakekeeper generic tables with the Java client, writing directly to S3, GCS or Azure using vended credentials.
Validate Lakekeeper storage profiles and credentials before you save them: the validation endpoints, every check they run, warnings for CORS and STACKIT bucket policies, and probe timeouts.
pylakekeeper, the official Python client for Lakekeeper's Generic Table API: catalog CRUD, OAuth2 authentication and vended storage credentials.

frontmatter.description: Attach governance tags such as pii or sensitivity=restricted to warehouses, namespaces, tables, views, generic tables and columns for classification, discovery and, with Cedar in Lakekeeper Plus, access control.
Bootstrap a new Lakekeeper deployment through the UI or the /management/v1/bootstrap endpoint. What initial access this grants depends on the configured authorizer.
Checklist for running Lakekeeper in production: database, storage, identity provider, authorization and high-availability recommendations.
Choose and configure a Lakekeeper Authorizer — OpenFGA or Cedar — and learn how grants, privileges and roles control access to catalog objects.
Common Lakekeeper problems and their causes: unexpected 403 responses, Helm and UI issues, and other frequently hit edge cases.
Configure Lakekeeper instance admins — principals from static configuration that bypass the Authorizer for administrative operations.
Configure Lakekeeper's structured JSON logging and RUST_LOG filtering, and understand the fields emitted by the tracing pipeline.
Configure admission gates in Lakekeeper Plus to allow or deny authenticated requests before they reach a handler, using an external entitlement service.
Contribute to Lakekeeper: development setup, pull request and CI expectations, conventional commits, and the contributor licence agreement.
Extend Lakekeeper in Rust: swap backends and implement traits and hooks for authorization, secret storage, event publishing and custom endpoints.
Grant, list and revoke a single privilege for one principal on one resource with Lakekeeper's authorizer-independent Grants API.
How Lakekeeper maintains Iceberg tables: metadata file cleanup, and in Lakekeeper Plus expire snapshots, optimize and remove orphan files.
Interactive OpenAPI reference for the Lakekeeper Management API: projects, warehouses, users, roles and permissions.
Lakekeeper Plus optimize keeps Iceberg tables fast to read: after writes it compacts small data files, applies delete files and merges small manifests, per warehouse or per table.
Lakekeeper's DEFINER and INVOKER view security models, and how the referenced-by view chain decides whose permissions are checked.
Lakekeeper's architecture and core concepts: projects, warehouses, namespaces, tables and views, and the external dependencies the catalog builds on.
Monitor Lakekeeper with Prometheus metrics and per-project endpoint statistics, and wire them into a Kubernetes, Prometheus and Grafana stack.
Policy-as-code authorization for Lakekeeper Plus with Cedar: declarative policies with attribute conditions, evaluated without an external service.
Reference for Lakekeeper's environment variables: database, storage, authentication, authorization, logging, routing and server settings.

Run Lakekeeper Plus optimize workers: with the Helm chart or on your own, how a run gets its memory, cores and spill disk, how size classes match tasks to worker pods, and how to stop a worker without losing work.
Run Lakekeeper task workers as Kubernetes Jobs that KEDA starts only while tasks wait: setup, database connections, leftover files and alerting.
Run Lakekeeper's authorization on OpenFGA for hierarchical, inheritable permissions across warehouses, namespaces, tables and views.
Secure Lakekeeper with OpenID Connect, OAuth 2 or Kubernetes service accounts, and map identity provider tokens to catalog users and roles.
Use the Lakekeeper OPA bridge to enforce catalog permissions in Trino and other engines that delegate access control to Open Policy Agent.
